subject: physics
title: Measuring length, volume and time
key_idea: Use a ruler or measuring cylinder with your eye at the right position, and a clock or timer for time. To find a very small distance or a very short time, measure many together and divide, so the reading error is shared out.

blocks.text: A ruler measures length and a measuring cylinder measures the volume of a liquid. This section covers how to read each one accurately.

items.meaning: A wrong reading caused by looking at a scale from an angle.
The curved surface of a liquid in a narrow tube.

items: Put the ruler **close to** the object, so the scale touches what you are measuring.
View the scale from directly in front, at right angles, to avoid **parallax error**.
Check that the ruler is straight along the object (use a set-square to check it is vertical).
Length is measured in metres (m), centimetres (cm) or millimetres (mm).
Stand the cylinder on a flat, level surface.
Put your eye level with the liquid surface.
Read the **bottom of the meniscus**. The volume between the bottom and the top of the curve is very small.
Volume is measured in cm³ (1 cm³ is the same as 1 ml).
Look at right angles to the scale to avoid parallax error.
Read a measuring cylinder at the bottom of the meniscus, on a level surface.

blocks.text: Clocks and timers measure time intervals. Pick the one that suits the length of the interval.

items: A **clock** or watch is suitable for long intervals, such as minutes or hours.
A **stopwatch** or digital timer is suitable for short intervals. A digital timer can read to 0.01 s.
Your reaction time (about 0.2 s) causes an error in every hand-timed reading. The error matters most for short intervals.
Keep the timer and the experiment close together, so you can see both.
Start and stop the timer at the same point in the motion each time.
To record a reading at an exact time, set a timer to go off at that time, or let a second person read the instrument.
Use a clock for long intervals and a stopwatch or digital timer for short ones.
Reaction time is the main error in hand-timed short intervals.

blocks.text: One very small distance or one very short time is hard to measure well. Measure many together and divide.

blocks.label: Average of multiples
where: total measurement is the whole length (m) or time (s)
number measured is the count of sheets, oscillations and so on

items: To find the thickness of one sheet of paper, measure a stack of 100 sheets and divide by 100.
To find the **period** of a pendulum, time 10 or 20 complete oscillations and divide by that number.
Start and stop the timer as the pendulum passes the same point, such as the middle of its swing.
Repeat the whole measurement and take an average.

items.meaning: One complete swing out and back to the starting position.
The time taken for one complete oscillation, in seconds.

blocks.text: Timing many oscillations is more accurate than timing one. The same timing error is spread over a longer time, so it is a smaller part of the result.

diagram.alt: A practice question. Find the period of a pendulum from the time for several oscillations.
diagram.question: A student times {n} complete oscillations of a pendulum. The total time is {t} s. Calculate the period of the pendulum.
working: period = total time ÷ number of oscillations

items: Measure many, then divide, to find a small distance or short time.
Timing many oscillations reduces the effect of reaction-time errors.

checks.q: Describe how to read the volume of water in a measuring cylinder accurately.
checks.a: Stand it on a level surface, put your eye level with the liquid and read at the bottom of the meniscus.

checks.q: Explain why timing 10 oscillations of a pendulum gives a more accurate period than timing one.
checks.a: The timing (reaction time) error is spread over a longer time, so it has less effect on the period.

checks.q: A stack of 200 sheets of paper is 2.0 cm thick. Calculate the thickness of one sheet.

worked_example.question: A student investigates the behaviour of a spring. She suspends a mass of 100 g from the spring and measures the stretched length of the spring. Describe two techniques for measuring the length of the spring, to ensure an accurate reading.
answer_points: Read the ruler viewing it perpendicularly (at right angles).
Put the ruler close to the spring.
Use a set-square or short ruler to measure the length of the spring.
Use a set-square to check that the ruler is vertical.
worked_example.tip: Any two score one mark each. Name the technique, not just "be careful".
